english.title: Aid / abet driving of a motor vehicle on a road / public place when alcohol level above the prescribed limit

english.legislation: Contrary to section 5(1)(a) of the Road Traffic Act 1988,Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act 1988 and section 44 of the Magistrates' Courts Act 1980.

other.powersofarrest:
Under section 6D of the Road Traffic Act 1988, if -
6D(1) A constable may arrest a person without warrant as a result of a preliminary breath test the constable reasonable suspects that the proportion of alcohol in that persons' breath or blood exceeds the prescribed limit.
6D(2) A constable may arrest a person without warrant if -
(a) the person fails to co-operate with a preliminary test in pursuance of a requirement imposed under section 6, and (b) the constable reasonably suspects that the person has alcohol or a drug in his body or is under the influence of a drug.
(c) A person may NOT be arrested under this section while in a hospital as a patient.
other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Obligatory disqualification and endorsement.

Obligatory endorsement - licence endorsed three to eleven penalty points - only if special reasons apply.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
